subject: Urgent: Seawind hosted API — p95/p99 latency spike and tokens-per-second collapse after runtime change
messages:
From: Jordan Liu <jordan.liu@seawind.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@seawind.ai
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden p95/p99 spike + tokens/sec collapse after your update — urgent

Hi Laura,

We saw a sharp regression in p95 and p99 latency starting ~08:30 PST this morning after the update you rolled to the hosted runtime. Our dashboards show a >3x increase in p99 and a 60% drop in tokens-per-second on our production routes. Our app is timing out user requests and we’re receiving many 502/503 errors.

We rely on Redwood’s hosted API for our autocomplete and chat flows — this is impacting live users. I attached a small bundle of request traces and a sampling of failing request IDs. Can someone confirm if there was a config/quantization or kernel selector change around that window?

We need an ETA for mitigation and whether you can rollback to the prior release. If this requires executive attention for credits or a formal SLA exception, please let us know.

Thanks,
Jordan Liu
Head of ML Engineering
Seawind AI

Attachments: error-snaps.zip (sample traces), perf-logs-20280618.tar.gz (server-side logs)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Jordan Liu <jordan.liu@seawind.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 09:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 spike + tokens/sec collapse after your update — urgent

Jordan —

Thanks for the quick flag and the logs. Immediately logging this as Sev 1. We're pausing the canary for the kernel selector rollout and spinning up diagnostics. Rishi and Markus are on initial triage; Monica will coordinate customer comms and any credits if required.

Next steps I already initiated:
- Paused the runtime rollout at 08:45 PST (prevents further traffic on new kernel selection policy)
- Starting a targeted rollback in the next 10m for routes matching Seawind’s account (will route traffic to the last verified kernel/quant profile)
- Rishi to confirm whether the quantization profile change was included with the canary (I don’t think so, but need confirmation)

We’ll update you with immediate telemetry and an ETA within 30 minutes. I’ve cc’d our operations and runtime leads.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: jordan.liu@seawind.ai
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 09:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 spike + tokens/sec collapse after your update — urgent

Quick triage notes (initial):
- Confirmed: kernel-selector policy v2.3.1 was rolled to 10% canary at 08:22 PST and increased to 25% at 08:35 PST. That policy includes a fallback mapping that prefers a lower-latency kernel for long sequences but appears to select a slower kernel for the short-sequence distribution that Seawind runs most heavily.
- Metrics: tokens/sec for their primary route dropped from ~4200 t/s to ~1600 t/s for the affected shards; p99 increased from ~210ms to ~950ms.
- Quantization: No explicit quant profile change was deployed to hosted API at that exact time, but the kernel selector picks different execution paths that interact poorly with the existing 4-bit quant profile for certain attention kernels.
- Immediate action: Started a scoped rollback of the selector rules for Seawind's model shards (in progress). Also enabling forced kernel pinning to the verified kernel while we analyze per-layer latency characteristics.

I’m collecting detailed traces and will post a zipped trace bundle to the Drive link. If rollback succeeds, we’ll measure for 2x traffic to validate behavior under load.

— Rishi
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: jordan.liu@seawind.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 spike + tokens/sec collapse — update and plan

Update: rollback completed for Seawind routing at 09:58 PST; traffic is back on the verified kernel. Preliminary telemetry: p95 trending down, tokens/sec recovering toward baseline but not fully recovered under peak load — still ~85% of previous t/s.

We discovered two contributing factors:
1) Kernel selector rule evaluated sequence-length percentile with a stale histogram (edge bucket skewed), causing an inappropriate kernel choice for short requests.
2) The kernel that was chosen has a slower per-token throughput under our 4-bit quant profile due to inefficient fused GEMM path on the current GPU driver (driver version 550.18).

Short-term mitigation: pin to verified kernel + force older driver affinity for affected pools (rolled back in the next 30m). Medium-term: adjust selector to bias toward measured t/s for each route and add a canary metric for tokens/sec in the rollout gates.

Asking Ops to validate end-to-end and confirm if we should issue a customer credit. Monica, can you lead the customer comms? I recommend we offer 1 week of service credit and a post-mortem within 48 hours.

— Markus
VP, Runtime Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Jordan Liu <jordan.liu@seawind.ai>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 spike + tokens/sec collapse after runtime change — temporary mitigation active

Jordan —

Thanks again for the traces. We completed a scoped rollback and kernel pin, and we’re observing recovery across your routes. Summary:
- Rollback complete (09:58 PST) and kernel pin established; tokens/sec recovering toward baseline
- Root causes identified: selector logic skew + interaction with a slower kernel path under current quant profile and GPU driver version
- Immediate mitigation: forced kernel pin + driver affinity rollback to previous build for the affected pool

Next steps:
- We’ll run a controlled A/B validation for 2 hours and then ramp traffic while monitoring tokens/sec and p99/p95.
- We will prepare a formal post-mortem and a permanent selector patch that includes tokens/sec as a canary metric; target delivery within 72 hours.
- Monica will surface formal credit proposal (we are proposing 1 week of service credit and a waived incident fee).

I’ll keep you updated every 2 hours during recovery. Apologies for the disruption — we’re treating this with highest priority.

— Laura
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Liu <jordan.liu@seawind.ai>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 13:52:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Seawind incident — credit proposal and next steps

Jordan —

First, thank you for your patience. We’d like to offer Seawind the following:
- One week of service credit applied to your account (SW-2028-501)
- A technical post-mortem within 48 hours that includes change timeline, root cause, and corrective actions
- Priority engineering time to validate your production model under our updated selector rules before they go broad

Please confirm acceptance of the credit and whether you want us to open a formal SLA exception ticket for downstream billing and procurement. If you need an expedited DocuSign for an addendum, we can prioritize that.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachment: seawind-sla-credits-request.pdf

From: Jordan Liu <jordan.liu@seawind.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@seawind.ai
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Seawind incident — credit proposal and post-mortem

Monica / Laura —

We appreciate the quick rollback and the credit offer. We accept the one week of service credit and would like the post-mortem shipped to our security contact and procurement (procurement@seawind.ai) and copied to our ML lead. Also please include any mitigation steps that will prevent this for short-sequence-heavy customers.

Two asks:
1) Please include the exact driver versions and kernel mappings that were changed so our infra team can cross-check with our internal telemetry.
2) We’d like a short runbook we can share with our SREs that lists how to detect tokens/sec regressions and recommended temporary client-side mitigations while Redwood is troubleshooting (e.g., reduce client-side batch size, short-circuit for small requests, retry window guidance).

Will wait for the post-mortem and the runbook. Thanks for the quick handling.

— Jordan
Head of ML Engineering
Seawind AI
